recommended_title: How Few Edits Displace the Top of a Bradley-Terry Leaderboard? A Verified First-Order Influence Attack Across Crowd, Expert, LLM-Judge and Sports Comparison Data
central_question: How many edits (0.1% to 2% of comparison rows, by dropping or flipping) does it take for a first-order influence search to dethrone the rank-1 competitor of a ridge Bradley-Terry leaderboard, and does that vulnerability differ across evaluation designs (crowd votes, expert human judgments, LLM-judge judgments, sports results)?
central_thesis: Under evaluator-verified exact refits, a single one-shot first-order influence edit search yields very different rank-1 vulnerability across evaluation designs: it displaces rank 1 in every crowd-vote and sports case at the 2% budget but in none of the LLM-judge cases and only in the flip mode for expert-human judgments; this is a measured, bounded result for one attack and one target (rank 1), not a general sensitivity law, and no improved search method was established.
narrative_rationale: The only completed, scored evidence is the sealed final evaluation of the frozen selection, which is the original first-order influence starter (selection_kind=baseline, investigation_outcome=completed_no_winner). All three attempted improved search variants were unscored (infrastructure failures), so they are missing evidence, not losses, and cannot support any improvement claim. The final evaluation is qualified/completed and gives (i) a family-averaged edit success of 0.606, (ii) per-design scores (crowd 1.000, sports 0.833, expert-human 0.374, LLM-judge 0.216), (iii) per-design/per-mode top-1 displacement rates at the largest budget, (iv) aggregate evaluator-owned baselines (random 0.071, constant 0.071, win-rate heuristic 0.574), (v) a permuted-input control gap of 0 and a valid proposal rate of 1. This supports a measurement paper whose message is heterogeneity across evaluation designs under a verified attack, with explicit scope limits. A method-improvement narrative would be unsupported; a negative-results framing about the tested method (no improvement over the baseline was established; margin versus the best baseline is 0 because the selected method is the influence baseline) is honest and still informative. The three-way contrast (human crowd vs. MT-Bench human vs. MT-Bench GPT-4 judge vs. NBA) directly answers the task's cross-design question.
edit_framing_decision: Not in edit mode: no prior manuscript exists. A fresh thesis-first framing was chosen over a method-improvement story (rejected because no variant was scored) and over a noise-vs-intent sensitivity story (rejected because the artifacts contain no noise-calibration or subsampling experiments).
staged_input_impact: No staged prior paper or new program inputs; downstream_study shows the frozen selection is byte-identical to the baseline (same program tree hash), so there is a single studied method.

Three attempted variants (re-linearised greedy, pair-class multi-rival greedy, rival-chunked prefix line search) have 0 scored attempts of 3; they appear at most as one sentence in limitations/supplement as unscored design attempts with no performance evidence.

method_groups.name: First-order influence edit search (studied method; frozen selection)
method_groups.include_reason: It is the only method with scored evidence. One ridge-BT fit, a sensitivity direction for the top-vs-runner-up gap via the penalised-Hessian solve, then rank rows by first-order gap change for drop or flip. Present it as the object of study, not as a novel contribution.

method_groups.name: Evaluator-owned reference edit policies: constant, random, win-rate heuristic
method_groups.include_reason: Give scale to the scores: constant and random sit near 0.071, win-rate near 0.574 (family-averaged). Only aggregate values are available; per-family baseline values must not be invented.

method_groups.name: Verification controls: exact trusted refit, permuted-input control, valid-proposal rate
method_groups.include_reason: Justify that scores are not self-reported (the evaluator refits the edited data) and that results are not an artifact of row order or identity (permuted-input gap 0; valid proposal rate 1.0).

method_groups.name: Unscored improved-search variants
method_groups.include_reason: Optional one-paragraph disclosure only (3 attempted, 0 scored); no comparison is drawn.

results_focus: Per-design edit success of the influence search (crowd 1.000, sports 0.833, expert-human 0.374, LLM-judge 0.216; equally weighted mean 0.606), sealed final scope.

Top-1 displacement rate at the largest (2%) budget by design and mode: crowd 1/1 (drop/flip), sports 1/1, expert-human 0 (drop) / 1 (flip), LLM-judge 0/0. State that rates are averages over cases and seeds and take only values 0 or 1 here.

Reference scale: constant 0.071, random 0.071, win-rate heuristic 0.574 vs influence 0.606; margin versus the best baseline is computed as 0 for the method as frozen (explain: the studied method is the influence baseline itself, so this is a consistency check, not a comparison).

Validity checks: permuted-input control gap 0.0, valid proposal rate 1.0, qualification outcome qualified with status completed; three evaluation seeds give identical scores (deterministic proposer; seeds relabel episodes only), so there is no between-seed variance to report and no confidence interval is available.

Contrast of the two MT-Bench judge types (expert human vs GPT-4 judge) as a within-source comparison; flag that the data sources differ in gap sizes and row counts and the cause of the difference is untested (do not claim a mechanism).

Separate search from final: search-scope baseline score 0.914 with delta 0.0, 3 of 3 variant attempts unscored; search and sealed-final scores are different scopes and must not be compared or averaged.
figure_plan: Overview schematic (page 1-2): comparison rows -> ridge BT fit -> top vs runner-up gap -> edit budget k (0.1%-2%) by drop or flip -> trusted refit -> edit success score, with the four evaluation designs shown as inputs.

Two-panel bar figure: (a) edit success by evaluation design for the influence search; (b) family-averaged edit success for constant, random, win-rate heuristic, influence search. Annotate that panel (b) baselines are aggregate only.

Table (not figure): top-1 displacement rate at the 2% budget by design x mode, plus scores; and a setup table listing the four designs, data sources, and cases (crowd: 1 case per mode; expert-human and LLM-judge: MT-Bench; sports: NBA seasons 2008, 2012, 2015).

figure_specs.purpose: Glance-value overview of the studied object: pairwise comparison data from four evaluation designs, BT fit, bounded drop/flip edits, exact-refit verification and the edit success score.
figure_specs.layout_rationale: The ICLR template is single-column (about 5.5 in text width); a left-to-right flow with 5-6 labelled boxes needs the full text width to keep labels at or above ~8 pt. Place on page 1 or 2.

figure_specs.purpose: Show heterogeneity of edit success across evaluation designs and give the evaluator reference scale (constant, random, win-rate heuristic).
figure_specs.layout_rationale: Two side-by-side panels with 4 bars each and category labels like 'LLM judge' and 'win-rate heuristic' need full text width in a single-column template; no shrinking. Use one colour for the studied method across both panels, muted grey for baselines, y-axis 0 to 1, values printed on bars.

supplementary_plan.purpose: Give the reproducibility and protocol depth that a reviewer would otherwise ask for without hiding anything essential to the thesis: the exact evaluation specification, metric definitions, the complete metric table, and the disclosure of the unscored search attempts.

planned_subsections.heading: Evaluator specification and metric definitions
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Ridge BT objective (tie = half a win, ridge 0.5e-3*sum t^2, gradient tolerance 1e-10), rank-1 target, gap definition, per-level score (1 if rank 1 displaced else clipped gap closure 1 - gap_after/gap_before), five budgets (0.1%, 0.25%, 0.5%, 1%, 2% of rows, k = max(1, ceil(f n))), equal family weights 0.25, definition of displacement rate at the largest budget, wire protocol and 30 s call limit. Derive from the task contract and evaluator description only.

planned_subsections.heading: Full final-evaluation metric table
planned_subsections.grounded_content: All retained sealed-final metrics: four design scores, eight design x mode displacement rates, four baseline totals, margin versus best baseline, permuted-input gap, valid proposal rate.

planned_subsections.heading: Seeded runs and evaluation evidence
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Three evaluation seeds (201, 202, 203) with identical scores, per-run durations, and the note that diagnostics of the candidate were marked unverified by the evaluator; explain what that does and does not imply.

planned_subsections.heading: Search-stage context and unscored variants
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Frozen selection equals the starter (selection kind baseline), search-scope baseline score and zero delta, 3 total / 0 scored / 3 unscored attempts; brief description of the three attempted variant designs as unevaluated, with the statement that unscored attempts are missing evidence rather than losses; search and final scopes differ.

planned_subsections.heading: Algorithm description of the first-order influence search
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Step-by-step description (ridge BT Newton fit, sensitivity direction from the penalised Hessian solve for the top-minus-runner-up gap, per-row first-order effect for drop and flip, selection of the k most gap-reducing rows with deterministic tie-breaking, restriction to decisive rows for flip) taken from the frozen program source.

planned_subsections.heading: LLM usage statement
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Required ICLR disclosure of the role of LLMs in ideation, code generation and writing in this automated pipeline, stated without identifying information.

notes_for_writer: Honesty first: the studied method is the first-order influence starter, selected as the frozen baseline with search delta 0.0 and margin versus the best baseline 0.0. The paper is a measurement and limitations paper. Do not claim a new method or any improvement, and do not call the influence search a contribution of the paper.

Final qualification facts come from final.qualification.*: outcome qualified, status completed, correct true. No qualification failure occurred, so do not describe a failed qualification. Still state that qualification is a validity gate (complete run, valid proposals, controls) and does not mean superiority or generalisation. Candidate diagnostics trust is 'unverified'; mention it in limitations.

Reader-facing metric names: 'edit success score' (per-budget score 1 if rank 1 is displaced else clipped fraction of the top-vs-runner-up gap closed, averaged over five budgets, then over cases and designs); 'top-1 displacement rate at the 2% budget' for the flip_rate_* quantities (avoid the word 'flip rate' unqualified because 'flip' is also an edit mode); 'family-averaged edit success' for the headline mean (0.606); 'evaluation design' for crowd / expert human / LLM judge / sports. Never print combined_score, rubric, eligible, or correctness rate.

Each metric must be traced to final.metric.* ids; the design-level numbers are the only per-design data available. No per-case, per-budget, per-model, gap-size, row-count or per-design baseline numbers are in paper_data.json, so do not state them. Dataset sizes may be described only qualitatively (arena crowd data is much larger than MT-Bench or per-season NBA data) unless the writer can cite a grounded source; avoid numeric row counts.

Uncertainty: three evaluation seeds give identical scores (0.6057 each), because the proposer is deterministic and seeds only relabel episodes. Say this plainly; it is not evidence of low sampling variance of the leaderboard data. No bootstrap or CI exists, so do not report any. Say displacement rates are 0/1-valued here.

Interpretation discipline: the ordering crowd > sports > expert human > LLM judge is measured for this attack and these final cases. Offer hypotheses (rank-1 margin relative to total data mass, concentration of influence in few pairs, number of competitors, tie handling) clearly labelled as untested; the artifacts include no experiment connecting them to the ordering. Do not describe the contrast as 'noise vs intentional manipulation'. Note that the attack is an upper-bound-style adversarial probe of a one-shot first-order heuristic, not a minimal-edit certificate: failure to displace rank 1 (LLM judge, expert drop) means this heuristic did not succeed within the budget, not that no successful edit set exists.

The win-rate heuristic (0.574) is close to the influence search (0.606) in family-averaged score; the 0.032 gap is a single evaluation value with no uncertainty estimate. Do not claim a reliable ranking of the two policies.

Search versus final: search-scope baseline score is 0.914 and sealed-final is 0.606; they cover different data and scopes, so state both only as separate facts and never as a decline or a generalisation gap. Attempts: 3 total, 0 scored, 3 unscored; unscored attempts are missing evidence, not measured losses. Do not mention infrastructure error causes beyond 'not scored'.

Related work: cite only keys present in references.bib (BT variants, ties, existence/consistency of MLE, ridge/penalised BT, uncertainty quantification). The bib does not currently include the dataset or robustness papers named in the task brief (Chatbot Arena, MT-Bench, influence functions, AMIP, vote rigging, leaderboard practices); describe such lines of work only if a bib entry exists, never invent a citation, and leave a gap rather than a fabricated reference. Do not search for or cite the excluded paper on dropping preferences to change top LLM rankings.

Placement and budgets (ICLR 2026, single column, body 8 to 9 pages, last page at least 75% full for 8-page bodies; double-blind; no URLs or names): plan roughly 1 page introduction with the overview figure, 1 page related work and background on BT with ridge and ties, 1.5 pages problem formulation and the attack and scoring protocol (objective, gap, edit modes, budgets, score hierarchy, controls), 0.5 page evaluation designs and data sources table, 2 pages results (design_scores figure, displacement-rate table, baselines, controls, seed behaviour), 1.5 pages analysis of what the evidence does and does not show (hypotheses labelled untested, within-MT-Bench contrast, relation of drop vs flip modes), 1 page limitations and scope. Fill with problem framing, derivation of the first-order effect, and limitation analysis rather than filler. If the substantive material cannot honestly fill 8 pages, prefer tightening within the allowed range over padding, and move protocol detail to the supplement as planned.

Include a limitations discussion covering: one attack (first-order, one-shot, single rival direction at the initial fit) and one target (rank 1) only; evaluator BT specification fixed (ridge, ties as half-win) so conclusions are tied to it; four designs with specific datasets (anonymised competitor labels; no noise-calibration, subsampling, or tie ablations were run); designs are confounded with dataset size, competitor count and gap size; NBA is not a preference/judge design; expert human and LLM judge share one source; no intent/noise attribution; no uncertainty over data sampling; diagnostics unverified; no improved search was established.

The task asked for reproduction code and checklist; in the paper, mention the evaluator specification so others can re-implement, but do not claim released scripts or runtimes unless they are in the artifacts. The ICLR LLM Usage section is mandatory and may sit in the appendix.

Overview figure uses generate-concept-figure (the single concept figure). The bar figure uses matplotlib, exports PDF and PNG at 300 DPI, and the LaTeX must include the PDF. Raster-only fallbacks need at least 2400 px width for full-width placement; never upscale a raster.

Readability budgets: design_scores has 2 panels, at most 4 categories and 1 series per panel; font at or above 8 pt at final size; keep each figure's threshold-style meaning single (the displacement rate is always 'at the 2% budget').
